q1_issues.issue: The similative adjunct "like wolves" is dropped entirely, although the instruction set explicitly licenses the surface-preposition oblique (Like …) for it.

q2_gaps: a parenthetical similative comparing the whole predication to another kind ("Pure dingoes, LIKE WOLVES, are …") — the one line licensing (Like …) does not say whether it attaches to the subject kind, to the (Skolem) event inside a generic rule, or to the proposition, and a kind-to-kind comparison of an entire claim has no shape at all

a three-word compound kind ("annual breeding cycle") — the decompose-once rule is stated for two-word modifier_noun pairs, so which of the two modifiers rides in the symbol and which gets a genus is left to judgment
notes: The generic bare-plural-to-Implication routing, the Skolem event, Patient on the passive subject, the Into oblique, the surface-form Manner adverb, the Still tag, and the 0.9/0.9 empirical generic TV are all correct. `pure_dingo` and `annual_breeding_cycle` are defensible fusions with the adjectival modifiers exposed and the noun modifier left unexposed, as the rule requires.
